tasks.short: Write and revise QC operating procedures

steps.what: Define required changes to standard quality control operating procedures and verify technical instructions
Write or revise procedure wording and cross-references from the specified technical changes

loop.purpose: Draft wording for human-defined procedure changes
loop.input: Current controlled procedure and checked change brief containing exact technical instructions and source references
loop.output: Draft revision and a trace from each change to its supplied instruction
loop.check: Analyst compares every instruction, sequence, limit, responsibility and warning with approved source material and checks that unchanged instructions retain meaning
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved wording or technical ambiguity returns to manual writing in this step
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates preserve headings but expressing variable technical instructions clearly requires writing; the model cannot invent methods or acceptance criteria

steps.what: Check procedure usability and technical meaning and accept the revision for controlled review

tasks.design: Use native controlled templates in {DOCS}, with a bounded loop drafting wording only from the analyst's verified change instructions. The analyst checks technical meaning and usability before submitting an exact revision to the existing controlled approval process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expressing already-decided technical changes consistently across a procedure took drafting time.
tasks.enabler_now: A constrained drafting loop can preserve document structure and expose changes for direct comparison with source instructions.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent instruction may change a method, sequence or responsibility in a consequential way.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows whether an operator could follow the procedure correctly and whether it represents the actual method.
tasks.altitude: A small wording gain after checking; technical ownership and controlled approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate approved analytical methods into unambiguous instructions

evidence.claim: The Novo Nordisk vendor case describes human-approved drafting of reports and verification protocols; this is adjacent documentation evidence, not a measured saving for QC procedures.
The proposed constrained procedure-wording workflow and small net saving are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is the analyst's procedure writing or revision and review submission, excluding analytical method development, formal quality approval, release, staff training and implementation. Those existing activities keep their owners and time.

Method owners supply approved source methods through unchanged technical work. Analyst defines and captures procedure version, change locations, exact intended technical instructions, source references, sequence, limits, responsibilities, warnings and protected wording in s1's 30 hours. No free structured technical brief is assumed.

s2 retains 26 hours for source-by-source checking and manual rewriting; missing technical decisions stop drafting and return to the analyst. The loop never selects limits, invents a step or decides that a procedure is compliant.

Try native templates and tracked changes first. s3's 30 hours retain usability and technical review. Existing quality owners approve or reject the submitted revision afterwards through unchanged work; 3 additional review hours are counted below.
unknowns: Whether controlled documents may be processed by the proposed tool
How much revision effort is wording versus unresolved technical decisions
Applicable quality validation and approval requirements
research_questions: Does draft assistance reduce writing after every instruction and unchanged section is checked against approved source material?

already_counted.description: Check the drafted instructions and manually rewrite uncertain wording

incremental.description: Maintain procedure drafting constraints and audit meaning changes
Additional quality-owner review of assisted revisions

approvals.approved_version: Exact review-submission revision, source method versions, change trace and unresolved questions; edits void acceptance and require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=86, gross=14; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=6. Range assumes frequent manual rewriting and unchanged technical review. Three other-role review hours are outside focal savings; no controlled approval or training effort is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in internal quality assessments and audits

steps.what: Review relevant quality records and prepare factual explanations for internal assessments and audits
Participate in internal assessments and audits and explain the evidence and uncertainties

tasks.design: Keep audit preparation and participation human, using existing records in {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the laboratory information management system. The analyst understands the evidence and answers questions about actual laboratory practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: An audit requires understanding and explaining evidence rather than merely collecting files.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native record access supports the task without a new summary layer.
tasks.still_hard: Questions may expose inconsistent practice, incomplete evidence or uncertainty that needs direct investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst explains what actually happened and recognises the limits of the evidence.
tasks.altitude: Audit participation time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain bench records and actual working practice
reach.learn: Evidence provenance and candid uncertainty reporting

evidence.claim: Internal audit participation requires human understanding and explanation of actual practice; no separate clerical saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the analyst's preparation and participation, excluding the auditor's planning, separate document administration and implementing corrective actions. Do not duplicate record creation or report drafting effort.

Quality record owners produce evidence through existing laboratory work. Auditor supplies scope before s1 and questions during s2, after preparation; analyst checks sources and captures explanations within the retained 100 hours. No free structured audit answer is assumed.
Keep current native record access. No model summary or new capture process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Audit scope and the analyst's expected participation
Which evidence gaps need separate investigation
research_questions: Can the analyst support each explanation with the actual controlled record and identify uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Understand audit evidence and participate in questioning and clarification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Preparation and audit conversation keep full effort; no auditor time or presumed file-copying baseline is included.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Interpret validation or transfer requirements and prepare the method work against applicable policies and guidelines
Perform method validations or transfers and evaluate actual performance against the approved work requirements

tasks.design: Keep method validation and transfer human, using the controlled plan in {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the laboratory analytical equipment and result system. The analyst prepares the work, observes actual method performance and records evidence for the existing method owner review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Method performance must be demonstrated under actual conditions rather than inferred from document completeness.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native plans and laboratory records already support the work; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected variation or differences between laboratories may need scientific investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises where the observed method behaviour conflicts with the intended use.
tasks.altitude: Validation or transfer effort and scientific responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Analytical method validation and transfer require actual work and scientific assessment; no saving is claimed for substituting document generation.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing and performing the assigned validation or transfer, excluding developing the method, authoring the master validation policy and formal final quality approval. Separately owned report or calculation actions must not be added twice.

Method owners provide the controlled method, plan and applicable policy references through existing work before s1. Analyst interprets them and captures operational preparation within s1's 40 hours; no free structured acceptance or validated-method flag is assumed.

Analyst and equipment produce observations during s2 before the corresponding performance evaluation. All handling, observation capture, interpretation and manual investigation remain in s2's 60 hours; instrument runtime earns no human saving.

Keep current native plans and records. No new tool, calculation pipeline or transfer of specialist work is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero; applicable quality requirements need customer confirmation.
unknowns: Whether the task is validation, transfer or both for the local methods
Which controlled plans and quality requirements apply
research_questions: Does the actual method evidence address the intended use and all required validation or transfer questions?

already_counted.description: Prepare and perform the method work, capture observations and investigate performance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Preparation, physical method work and scientific assessment retain full effort; no equipment runtime or quality-owner time is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Evaluate analytical methods and procedures using their actual performance and limitations
Determine how methods and procedures might be improved and identify required investigation

tasks.design: Keep analytical method evaluation human, using source evidence in {OTHER}, the laboratory information management system, and controlled procedures in {DOCS}. The analyst explains limitations and proposes investigations rather than automatically changing a method.
tasks.previous_blocker: A useful improvement must address scientific limitations without compromising the intended analytical use.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native performance records support review; no new recommendation engine is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Observed problems may arise from sampling, equipment, execution or the method itself.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst forms and tests plausible explanations rather than treating correlation as a method defect.
tasks.altitude: Method improvement evaluation and recommendation rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Scientific hypothesis testing and method trade-offs

evidence.claim: Evaluating analytical improvements requires scientific judgement; a generated recommendation does not establish a better method.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluating methods and suggesting improvements, excluding routine data compilation, executing experiments, formal method validation and controlled implementation. Shared analytical actions must have one owner.

Laboratory testing and prior investigations produce performance evidence through existing work before s1. Analyst reads, verifies and captures limitations within s1's 60 hours and develops recommendations within s2's 40 hours; no free structured root-cause or improvement score is assumed.

Recommendations remain proposals; existing method owners decide what to investigate afterwards through unchanged work. Keep native records and current review practice, with no new system or incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which method limitations are most consequential locally
What evidence distinguishes method effects from execution problems
research_questions: Does each proposed improvement state the observed limitation, alternative explanations and evidence needed to test it?

already_counted.description: Evaluate method evidence and develop scientific improvement recommendations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Scientific evaluation and recommendation retain full time; no routine data-pipeline saving is counted again.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Carefully constrained procedure wording may save a little time, while audits, method validation and scientific improvement judgement remain human.
reach: Study method intent and limitations with chemists
Examine actual bench practice with chemical technicians
skills_to_grow: Specify exact technical changes before drafting
Check procedure meaning and operational usability
role.ambitious_version: Maintain clear, controlled instructions and sound analytical methods while keeping technical and quality decisions with responsible people.
